newsitem.title: THAILAND: Prospect of China buying pares Thai rubber losses.
newsitem.headline: Prospect of China buying pares Thai rubber losses.

text.p: Thai rubber prices continued to fall this week but sentiment started to strengthen on enquiries from China, traders said on Friday.
China was expected to buy soon as stocks at some of its factories were falling, said a trader at a firm with a big share of the Chinese market.
The Chinese made enquiries but placed no firm orders, traders said. "But they are expected to buy soon, within this month," said one trader.
"It's dead quiet this week after the baht float. But we expect China's presence to help lift the gloom soon, at least for the near term," he said.
Also, prices were approaching the INRO's may-buy level of 183 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg.

But these two factors were expected to help buoy the market only in the near term. Industry sources said rubber prices were likely to remain under pressure from underlying bearish factors and Thailand's floating of the baht on Wednesday.
The float pushed the value of the baht down by more than 10 percent and made prices of Thai commodities exports attractive.
Traders played down the impact of a rubber producers' rally in the south of Thailand, saying it barely affected the market.
About 600 rubber producers and rambutan growers staged a rally to demand more government help.
Some rubber planters said the government had so far bought no rubber from the province at guaranteed prices.
The government launched a price intervention scheme in May, under which it bought unsmoked sheet rubber grade 3 from the domestic market at 29.00 baht a kg ($1.03).
Thai benchmark RSS3 for August delivery was quoted around 87.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok. October was quoted at 97.50 cents and January at 91.50 on the same basis.
